title: Introduce Token Degradation Index and Alert Federation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a Token Degradation Index metric to help surface quality regressions tied to token-level signals; ships an Alert Federation layer to map SLO-level incidents to team-scoped alerts with intelligent suppression. Includes dashboards and migration guidance.
description: Motivation: We observe intermittent quality regressions that do not linearly correlate with latency or raw token cost. These manifest as higher downstream error rates or lower utility despite normal throughput. Existing token-level telemetry is fragmented (cost, latency, kv-cache misses, eval hooks) and noisy at high cardinality. This PR introduces a Token Degradation Index (TDI) — a composite metric that combines token-level cost, perplexity-proxy signals (from streaming eval hooks), and KV-cache effectiveness to surface short-lived degradations. In addition, it adds an Alert Federation layer that translates high-level SLO signals into team-scoped alerts with suppression and deduplication rules to reduce alert fatigue. Changes: - Telemetry: add metric "token.degradation_index" (gauge + histogram rollups), per-invocation tagging (route, model_version, tenant_id, prompt_shape_bucket). Add sampled enriched spans that include eval_hash and representative prompt snippet for long-tail inspections. - Tracing: enrich root spans with token.degradation_score and include a compact token fingerprint for trace correlation without leaking prompts. - Alerting: introduce federated alert rules (alerts/federation/rules.yaml) that accept a canonical incident and create scoped alerts for owning teams; add suppression for noise patterns (small-sample spikes and transient cache-warmups). - Dashboards: new "Token Degradation Explorer" with cohort filters (model_version, tenant, route), time-to-recovery panel, and a federated-alert view that shows which teams were notified for each incident. - Sampling & storage: introduce reservoir sampling for high-cardinality token samples and an adjustable retention configuration to keep a stratum of degraded invocations. - Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag observability.tdi.enabled; canary rollout to 10% of traffic, monitored for false positives for 72 hours before full roll. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and do not change existing names; alert federation is opt-in. Checklist: - [x] Add metric definitions and docs - [x] Implement server-side TDI computation and tagging - [x] Add trace enrichment with privacy-safe fingerprint - [x] Create dashboards and dashboard tests - [x] Add alert federation rules and unit tests - [x] Add integration tests and run canary - [x] Documentation and rollout playbook Files of interest: telemetry/metrics/token_metrics.go, tracing/enrichers/token_enricher.go, alerts/federation/rules.yaml, observability/dashboards/token_degradation_explorer.json, sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py, docs/observability/token-degradation.md, tests/integration/test_token_degradation.py, helm/values-observability.yaml Migration/rollout notes: deploy with observability.tdi.enabled=false; enable in canary (10%) and monitor token.degradation_index.hotcount and federated_alert.rate. If noise > 5% of alerts, pause and adjust sampling thresholds. Why this is different: unlike previous PRs that focused on cost or percentile rollups, this change fuses cross-cutting signals (cost, perplexity proxies, cache health) into a single index and couples it with an alerting federation that reduces noise while ensuring teams are paged when ownership matters.

review_comments: Priya: Can we avoid shipping raw prompt snippets in spans? Suggest storing only a hashed prefix and shape bucket. - author reply: We only include a 64-bit FNV fingerprint and a prompt_shape_bucket; updated token_enricher.go accordingly.
Liam: The default reservoir size seems high for high-cardinality tenants — can we expose per-tenant caps? - author reply: Added per-tenant reservoir caps and a global override in helm values.

Jamal: Alert federation should prefer dedupe over noisy-suppression for large tenants. Requested change: add tenant-weighted dedupe and escalate if suppression hides sustained degradation. - author reply: Implemented tenant-weighted dedupe and added a rate-based escalator in rules.yaml.
